generic_name: Ascorbic Acid and Tocopheryl Acid (Vitamin C and Vitamin E)
purpose: This combination provides your body with two important vitamins — Vitamin C and Vitamin E. These vitamins help support your immune system, protect your cells from damage, and promote overall health. They are also sometimes used to help with wound healing and skin health.
how_it_works: Both Vitamin C and Vitamin E are powerful antioxidants, which means they help protect your body's cells from damage caused by harmful molecules called free radicals. Think of them as tiny shields defending your cells every day. Vitamin C also helps your body make collagen, which keeps your skin, bones, and tissues strong and healthy.
common_side_effects: At normal doses, side effects are uncommon. However, taking too much Vitamin C can cause stomach upset, nausea, diarrhea, or stomach cramps. High doses of Vitamin E may occasionally cause headache, nausea, or fatigue. These effects usually go away if the dose is reduced.
warnings: Do not take more than the recommended dose, as very high amounts of Vitamin C can increase your risk of kidney stones. High doses of Vitamin E may increase bleeding risk, especially if you take blood thinners like warfarin. Always let your doctor know you are taking these vitamins, especially before any surgery or if you have kidney disease.
typical_dosing: Typical daily doses are around 65–2000 mg of Vitamin C and 15–1000 mg of Vitamin E for adults, depending on the reason for use. Always follow the label or your doctor's instructions. Take with food if you notice any stomach upset.
